accepted_scope_caveats.label: ass:deterministic-rate-limit and thm:local-minimax-lower-bound
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The lower envelope is conditional on the deterministic-limit procedure class; sequential, positive-pilot-fraction, and random-limit designs are excluded.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Local minimax optimality within the explicitly defined deterministic-limit pilot-annotation class.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: finite-support local experiment
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The LAN, efficient covariance, and attainment claims assume fixed finite strata, fixed finite outcome support, and an interior baseline.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The stated Gaussian minimax characterization for the finite-support randomized-annotation experiment.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:certified-computation
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Termination and enclosure are asserted only for rational-polytopal state sets and rational or real-algebraic inputs carrying exact validity certificates.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Certified approximation of V* on the represented-input domain, not for opaque real inputs or arbitrary compact sets.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper designs a second experimental wave for policy choice, proves asymptotic optimality through a Gaussian approximation, and requires welfare to be strongly concave near the optimum.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 1, lines 52–56; pp. 7–8, proportional two-batch setup and ATE definition
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper optimizes annotation probabilities for precision of average-treatment-effect estimation and uses a two-batch annotation design.
The paper studies model-free two-phase sampling based on semiparametric efficiency bounds and reduces a multidimensional componentwise/maximin criterion to a tractable optimization.
The paper develops asymptotic optimality for statistical treatment rules through limit experiments under average and minimax risk criteria.
The paper establishes asymptotic minimax-regret optimality for many treatments and discusses computational game methods.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Sections 5–7; Gaussian-game discussion and binary special case
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies two-stage independent-arm best-arm identification, develops a Gaussian minimax game, and records a binary Neyman-allocation reduction.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Prove a generic characterization of when pairwise-variance criteria agree with regret-optimal annotation, with the witness as the strict-failure branch rather than the sole geometric result.
Make the Kato comparator chain theorem-level: state precisely why no independent-arm allocation representation can preserve the overlapping loading covariance and nuisance kernel.
Determine whether m_n/sqrt(n)→∞ is necessary for the coupled selector; weaken it to the minimal pilot condition if the implementation proof only needs uniform consistency.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 on the deterministic-limit finite-support scope, prioritizing the coupled measurable-attainment construction and its minimal pilot-rate condition.
